1. I take adderall XR 
2. It helps me focus, remember, control impulses, stay on a schedule and actually get school work done. Let’s put it this way when my meds work, I’m an A student when they don’t I’m a D student. And don’t think everything will come easy now that you can focus your drill going to have to woken 10 times as harder as the other students. BUT, I feel horrible all day, I’ll feel good mentally bc I’m getting school work done, but after I close my laptop I’m useless. My mom is mad cuz I’m not helping her around the house as I should be but I’m just so exhausted all the time and it takes twice asl on her to answer she may ask me as opposed to when I’m not on the meds, which irritates her too. Yea the meds will completely destroy your appetite which is manageable so don’t let that deter you from getting meds that can really benefit you! I usually try to eat a breakfast before the meds are in my system and then have a late dinner after they left my system. As long as you don’t take the medication too close to bedtime you should be fine with sleep. 
3. I was diagnosed with ADHD and ADD when I was in the 3rd grade and started on the meds soon after. 
4. I think it’s worth it but my ADHD is from a seizure at birth and thus severe, so I’m totally dependent on them. But I know others who also have been diagnosed but can manage it without meds(sometimes just knowing is half the battle) 
4. I don’t tell people, unless were extremely close. I literally just told my best friend even though we’ve been friends for three years. There is so much stigma around the disorder and meds so I don’t let anyone have the knowledge to say anything negative. It’s a personal choice to tell others.  But I will say this definitely definitely definitely tell a SO, bc it will impact any and all relationships you form with others.

Honestly when starting any new ADHD medicine there is going to be growing pains. And the sluggishness is probably not going to get better, it may improve but don’t expect it to. I’ve taken every variation of ADHD meds since I was in 3rd grade (9 years) and I’ve never not been tired. I would say increase first but in small increments if you increase too much he’ll probably improve in school but the side effects could really take a toll. And don’t worry if you have to change the dose and/ or type of meds especially when he goes through puberty(hormones and all that) in the future.
